exposure: NICU type (Type A with restrictions, Type A, Type B, Type C)
outcome: gestational age-specific composite quality measures (Baby-MONITOR for extremely and very preterm infants, adapted MLP quality measure for MLP infants)
cohort: The study included 433,814 premature infants (376,219 moderate and late preterm, and 57,595 extremely and very preterm) born in 465 US hospitals between 2016 and 2020, without anomalies, who survived more than 12 hours and were transferred no more than once.
finding: Composite quality scores were lower for moderate and late preterm infants in type C NICUs, while extremely and very preterm composite quality scores were similar across all NICU types.
